plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional shaded rendering of two surfaces intersecting above a labeled coordinate frame. The vertical axis rises from an origin marked 0, the y-axis runs off to the right, and the x-axis comes forward toward the lower left carrying a tick labeled 2. A downward-opening paraboloid forms a wide cap, shaded blue around its outer rim and warming to orange at the crown; a straight arrow at the upper right points to it from the label z = 4 - x squared - y squared. Rising through the cap is a vertical circular cylinder rendered in blue with a hollow open top, its wall cut off by the paraboloid so that the two meet along a closed curve high on the surface. The base of the cylinder is drawn as an ellipse lying in the xy-plane, touching the origin on one side and reaching out to the tick at 2 on the other, and a curved arrow from below points to it from the label (x - 1) squared + y squared = 1. Nesting the cylinder inside the cap makes visible exactly which portion of the paraboloid stands above the circular disk. The rendering sets up a volume calculation for the solid bounded below by that disk and above by the paraboloid.

vertical circular cylinder (x - 1)² + y² = 1 (center (1,0), radius 1) rising through the cap, rendered as an open-top semi-transparent blue wall
closed intersection curve where the cylinder wall meets the paraboloid, high on the surface
base disk (x - 1)² + y² = 1 lying in the xy-plane, touching the origin and reaching x = 2

origin marker labeled 0

interactions.label: Bounding surface
interactions.teaches: The volume is enclosed by exactly three surfaces — the cap above, the cylinder wall around the side, and the disk below — and the closed curve where cap and wall meet defines the top rim of the solid

interactions.label: Slice height z
interactions.teaches: A horizontal slice at height z cuts the solid in a disk (or disk clipped by the cap) whose radius shrinks as z approaches the paraboloid, so the volume is the accumulation of these shrinking cross-sections

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The 2D disk (x - 1)² + y² = 1 in the xy-plane is the region of integration; extruding it upward until it hits z = 4 - x² - y² produces the 3D solid, connecting the xy-region to the z-integration bounds 0 ≤ z ≤ 4 - x² - y²

interactions.label: Bounding surfaces
interactions.teaches: Editing the cap height or shifting the cylinder center redraws the wall, disk, cap, and their intersection, showing how the enclosed volume and its integration bounds depend on both equations

demo_steps.title: Base region
demo_steps.narration: Start with just the disk (x - 1)² + y² = 1 in the xy-plane, centered at (1,0) with radius 1 — it touches the origin and reaches the tick at x = 2. This is the region of integration.

demo_steps.title: Extrude to the cap
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the capped solid: the disk rises as a vertical cylinder until its wall meets the paraboloid z = 4 - x² - y² along a closed curve. The solid lives below the cap and inside the wall.

demo_steps.title: Sweep a slice upward
demo_steps.narration: Raise the slice from z = 0 toward z = 3. Near the base the cross-section is the full disk; as z climbs, the paraboloid clips it on the side nearer the origin, so slices shrink — their accumulation is the volume.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: paraboloid z = 4 - x² - y² with vertex at (0,0,4), drawn for radius up to ~2.2 (skirt near z ≈ 0), so the whole figure spans x ∈ [-2.2, 2.2], y ∈ [-2.2, 2.2], z ∈ [0, 4.2]. Cylinder: axis vertical through (1,0), radius 1, wall from z = 0 up to where it meets the cap; its base disk touches the origin and extends to x = 2 (matching the x-axis tick labeled 2). Axes: z vertical up from origin; y to the right; x forward toward the lower-left, with the tick '2' on the +x axis just past the disk edge. Orientation matches the source: cylinder sits left-of-center around the z-axis, its top rim (the intersection curve) tilts — higher on the far side from the origin, lower near the origin side. Colors from source: paraboloid gradient from steel blue #5b8fc4 at the rim to orange #d2691e / #e07b39 at the crown; cylinder wall translucent blue #7aa8d8 (opacity ~0.55) with a brighter blue rim at its open top; base disk flat blue #4f86c6; axes black with arrowheads; labels black. Intersection curve satisfies both equations: substitute (x-1)² + y² = 1, i.e. x² + y² = 2x, into the cap to get z = 4 - 2x along the curve — parametrize as x = 1 + cos t, y = sin t, z = 2 - 2 cos t. Slice at height z: cross-section is the set of (x,y) in the disk with x² + y² ≤ 4 - z (full disk when z ≤ 0-plane skirt region; clipped circular lens above).
interactionPlan.notes: Build the paraboloid as a ParametricGeometry over (r, θ) with vertex color gradient by height (blue→orange). Cylinder wall as an open-ended CylinderGeometry (openEnded) clipped at the cap by clipping each vertex z to 4 - x² - y², double-sided, transparent. Intersection curve as a THREE.Line loop using the closed-form parametrization above, drawn in a dark accent color (#cc3300) so it stays visible against both surfaces. For the slice slider, draw a translucent filled cross-section mesh recomputed each frame: intersection of disk(x=1,r=1) with disk(0, sqrt(max(0,4-z))) — a full circle, a circular lens, or empty. For 'Base region' view hide the cylinder wall and cap-intersection geometry and flatten to emphasize the disk (keep axes); for equation input, re-parse on change, show inline error text on parse failure, and rebuild wall/cap/intersection reactively. Keep both toggle-driven surface highlights as emissive boosts rather than swapping materials.

authoredContext:
Find the volume of the solid that lies under the paraboloid z=4−x2−y2 and above the disk (x−1)2+y2=1 on the xy-plane. See the paraboloid in the figure intersecting the cylinder (x−1)2+y2=1 above the xy-plane.

Finding the volume of a solid with a paraboloid cap and a circular base.

A paraboloid with equation z = 4 minus x squared minus y squared is intersected by a cylinder with equation (x minus 1) squared + y squared = 1.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional shaded rendering of two surfaces intersecting above a labeled coordinate frame. The vertical axis rises from an origin marked 0, the y-axis runs off to the right, and the x-axis comes forward toward the lower left carrying a tick labeled 2. A downward-opening paraboloid forms a wide cap, shaded blue around its outer rim and warming to orange at the crown; a straight arrow at the upper right points to it from the label z = 4 - x squared - y squared. Rising through the cap is a vertical circular cylinder rendered in blue with a hollow open top, its wall cut off by the paraboloid so that the two meet along a closed curve high on the surface. The base of the cylinder is drawn as an ellipse lying in the xy-plane, touching the origin on one side and reaching out to the tick at 2 on the other, and a curved arrow from below points to it from the label (x - 1) squared + y squared = 1. Nesting the cylinder inside the cap makes visible exactly which portion of the paraboloid stands above the circular disk. The rendering sets up a volume calculation for the solid bounded below by that disk and above by the paraboloid.

interactions.label: Bounding surface
interactions.teaches: The volume is enclosed by exactly three surfaces — the cap above, the cylinder wall around the side, and the disk below — and the closed curve where cap and wall meet defines the top rim of the solid

interactions.label: Slice height z
interactions.teaches: A horizontal slice at height z cuts the solid in a disk (or disk clipped by the cap) whose radius shrinks as z approaches the paraboloid, so the volume is the accumulation of these shrinking cross-sections

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The 2D disk (x - 1)² + y² = 1 in the xy-plane is the region of integration; extruding it upward until it hits z = 4 - x² - y² produces the 3D solid, connecting the xy-region to the z-integration bounds 0 ≤ z ≤ 4 - x² - y²

demo_steps.title: Base region
demo_steps.narration: Start with just the disk (x - 1)² + y² = 1 in the xy-plane, centered at (1,0) with radius 1 — it touches the origin and reaches the tick at x = 2. This is the region of integration.

demo_steps.title: Extrude to the cap
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the capped solid: the disk rises as a vertical cylinder until its wall meets the paraboloid z = 4 - x² - y² along a closed curve. The solid lives below the cap and inside the wall.

demo_steps.title: Sweep a slice upward
demo_steps.narration: Raise the slice from z = 0 toward z = 3. Near the base the cross-section is the full disk; as z climbs, the paraboloid clips it on the side nearer the origin, so slices shrink — their accumulation is the volume.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: paraboloid z = 4 - x² - y² with vertex at (0,0,4), drawn for radius up to ~2.2 (skirt near z ≈ 0), so the whole figure spans x ∈ [-2.2, 2.2], y ∈ [-2.2, 2.2], z ∈ [0, 4.2]. Cylinder: axis vertical through (1,0), radius 1, wall from z = 0 up to where it meets the cap; its base disk touches the origin and extends to x = 2 (matching the x-axis tick labeled 2). Axes: z vertical up from origin; y to the right; x forward toward the lower-left, with the tick '2' on the +x axis just past the disk edge. Orientation matches the source: cylinder sits left-of-center around the z-axis, its top rim (the intersection curve) tilts — higher on the far side from the origin, lower near the origin side. Colors from source: paraboloid gradient from steel blue #5b8fc4 at the rim to orange #d2691e / #e07b39 at the crown; cylinder wall translucent blue #7aa8d8 (opacity ~0.55) with a brighter blue rim at its open top; base disk flat blue #4f86c6; axes black with arrowheads; labels black. Intersection curve satisfies both equations: substitute (x-1)² + y² = 1, i.e. x² + y² = 2x, into the cap to get z = 4 - 2x along the curve — parametrize as x = 1 + cos t, y = sin t, z = 2 - 2 cos t. Slice at height z: cross-section is the set of (x,y) in the disk with x² + y² ≤ 4 - z (full disk when z ≤ 0-plane skirt region; clipped circular lens above).
interactionPlan.notes: Build the paraboloid as a ParametricGeometry over (r, θ) with vertex color gradient by height (blue→orange). Cylinder wall as an open-ended CylinderGeometry (openEnded) clipped at the cap by clipping each vertex z to 4 - x² - y², double-sided, transparent. Intersection curve as a THREE.Line loop using the closed-form parametrization above, drawn in a dark accent color (#cc3300) so it stays visible against both surfaces. For the slice slider, draw a translucent filled cross-section mesh recomputed each frame: intersection of disk(x=1,r=1) with disk(0, sqrt(max(0,4-z))) — a full circle, a circular lens, or empty. For 'Base region' view hide the cylinder wall and cap-intersection geometry and flatten to emphasize the disk (keep axes); for equation input, re-parse on change, show inline error text on parse failure, and rebuild wall/cap/intersection reactively. Keep both toggle-driven surface highlights as emissive boosts rather than swapping materials.
